passage.text: Bicycle sharing services have appeared in many Japanese cities. Users can unlock a bicycle with a smartphone and return it to any station in the city. Some companies place their stations near train stations and office buildings. In this way, they give commuters a choice other than crowded buses and trains. The number of users has increased quickly in the last few years.

illustrations.caption: 3コマ。①駅前でバス停の長い列を見る会社員の女性「The bus is always so crowded.」→ The next morning ②スマホでシェアサイクルの鍵を開ける → Three months later ③自転車で会社の前を走る。吹き出しに、他の会社員たちも同じ自転車に乗る様子。

narration.openingSentence: One morning, Ms. Mori was standing outside the station and looking at a long line at the bus stop.

questions.prompt: Please look at the passage. According to the passage, how do some companies give commuters a choice other than crowded buses and trains?
questions.modelAnswer: By placing their bicycle sharing stations near train stations and office buildings.

questions.prompt: Now, please look at the picture and describe the situation. You have twenty seconds to prepare. Your story should begin with the sentence on the card.
questions.modelAnswer: One morning, Ms. Mori was standing outside the station and looking at a long line at the bus stop. She said that the bus was always so crowded. The next morning, she was unlocking a rental bicycle with her smartphone. Three months later, she was riding the bicycle past her office. She was thinking that many other workers could also use the bicycles.

questions.prompt: Some people say that cities should build more roads for bicycles. What do you think about that?
questions.modelAnswer: I agree. Bicycles and cars on the same road are dangerous for both. Cities that built bicycle roads have fewer accidents, though it costs a lot of money.

questions.prompt: Today, many people are trying to reduce the amount of energy they use. Do you think people will use cars less in the future?

yes.modelAnswer: Cities are getting better public transport, and young people in cities do not even get a license.

no.modelAnswer: People in the countryside have no other way to move. Cars will only change from gasoline to electricity.
